principles.text: Being too early is not an edge for his style: it slowly drains mental and financial capital through repeated small losses, so by the time the real move comes he lacks the size or conviction to catch it.
Short-side moves are faster than long-side moves; if you miss the early entries you probably won't catch the move without chasing.
After a parabolic move, the bounce that forms the first lower high (a failed second attempt to push up after the first crack) is a decent short entry.
Prefers to short near the highs on a rebound (trying to hit the turn) and add when the stock/ETF confirms the breakdown; shorting after a close below the 9-period MA is also good.
Does not short on weakness in the first 15-30 minutes after the open (too volatile); waits for the intraday rebound into aligned resistance.

Whether to move a stop to breakeven depends on market stage: when he believes a downtrend is beginning he does not move short stops to breakeven and will sacrifice open profits to capture more downside.
In a market he doesn't expect to produce a multi-week rally, he closes longs as soon as they break the 9 EMA and the prior candle's low rather than giving room to the 21 EMA or breakeven.
Equity curve governs aggressiveness: when trading well he holds larger positions and takes fewer profits; in a drawdown he takes profits sooner and moves stops to breakeven.
On days/periods that are not in your favor, don't trade or trade less, because losses on bad days are what kill you.
Overly tight stops are not necessarily good; don't blindly copy his entries, stop placement or stock selection.
